summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to drive a multi-phase milestone (v2.0) to completion: verify/complete already-executing phases, discover and fix a manager display bug, then plan and execute several closeout phases (74–79) autonomously across quota resets, and finally ship Phase 74 through the full ship-phase gate pipeline.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 75, and 77 were verified/completed and merged or left ready for review; Phase 74 was planned, executed, and pushed through most of the ship-phase pipeline (verify/secure/crypto-review/security-review/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit) but a real desktop-e2e failure surfaced a genuine hex-vs-base64 encoding bug in the SC#2 grant re-mint plus a dirty-resume revocation-bypass gap, so PR #607 remains unmerged pending a gap-closure fix; Phases 76/78/79 were not started (76's empty branch was deleted).

repo: GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose case-insensitive substring match for 'PLAN' after the primary *-PLAN.md regex, so any doc file whose name merely contains 'PLAN' (e.g. '69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md' via 'write-PLANE') is miscounted as an extra plan, breaking implementation_complete/disk_status computation.
GSD's `is_active` phase flag just means 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' (init.cjs:1140) — it does not indicate a running agent.

The manager's completion predicate (`phase uat-passed --require-verification`) downgrades a phase to 'partial' if it has verification passed but no UAT.md artifact, even when human UAT was legitimately not applicable (e.g. Rust/FUSE phases verified via cargo test + CI).

The cipher-box share API wire contract (all 4 share DTOs: create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) validates encrypted key fields as hex via `@Matches(/^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/)`, while internal node-codec/sealed-ref storage uses base64 — these are two indistinguishable-at-the-type-level domains and mixing them (as Phase 74's FUSE re-mint did, sending base64 where hex was required) causes runtime 400s that mocked unit tests never catch — only the live desktop-e2e/sdk-e2e round-trip exercises it.

vitest does not load .env files, so SDK_E2E_SECRET must be explicitly exported in the shell before running sdk-e2e tests, or the harness silently falls back to a default secret and gets 401s against the real API.

Sub-agents launched from the repo root cannot use EnterWorktree to pin into an already-existing git worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree') — the working pattern for resuming background planner/executor work is to switch the main checkout to the feat branch directly and run agents there sequentially.

commit.gpgsign=false in this repo, so autonomous commits never block on 1Password biometric prompts; pre-commit hooks (lint-staged) are just slow (~1-2 min) and a 'timeout' on git commit usually means the commit landed — verify with git log, don't retry blindly.
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
Desktop E2E is dispatch-gated (not automatic on PR open) and must be triggered explicitly via workflow_dispatch against the branch.

code.finding: re_mint_grants_rooted_at base64-encodes the wrapped read key for the share grant's encrypted_read_key field, but the share API DTO validates that field as hex — causes 400 Bad Request and rotation fails closed at runtime (only caught by desktop-e2e, not unit tests).
SentShareResponse doc comments mislabel base64-encoded encrypted_read_key/encrypted_write_key fields as 'Hex-encoded' (lines 181, 183); item_name_encrypted at line 192 is correctly hex.

TS rotatedNodes map stores readKey by reference (aliased with parentNewReadKey) rather than cloning like Rust does, so a future zeroization change to parentNewReadKey could silently zero the returned map entry — latent, not yet triggered.

refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys runs before rotate_read_on_scope_exit returns Ok, ensuring all loaded inode nodes refresh before any relink/reseal — correctly closes the deep-intermediate stale-key bypass.

workflow: When a background/scheduled agent dies mid-task, verify actual on-disk state (git log, file listings, plan-checker verdicts) rather than trusting the agent's final reported message, which can understate progress already committed.

For long autonomous runs spanning quota resets, schedule a CronCreate resume with the exact corrected working method embedded in the prompt (not just 'continue') — and delete/replace the cron once the approach changes, or the next resume repeats a known-failed strategy.

Delegate heavy analysis-only gates (security audit, crypto review, simplify) to a sub-agent in parallel with a stack-dependent gate (SDK-E2E) run separately to avoid resource contention, since audit agents don't need the live docker stack.

The desktop-e2e/live-integration gate is valuable precisely because it catches real encoding/wire-contract bugs that mocked unit tests and typecheck cannot — don't skip it even when all other gates are green, especially for security/crypto-touching phases.

friction: Overnight background planners (74, 75, 77) all died to session quota limits before completing, requiring multiple resume cycles and re-diagnosis of partial state each time.

EnterWorktree could not be used from a sub-agent at repo root to resume work in a pre-existing worktree, forcing a pivot from parallel worktree-isolated planning to sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch processing, which serializes what was meant to be parallel work.
A CI Typecheck failure was found on Phase 74's PR (mock fixtures not updated for a widened RotateReadResult type) that unit tests didn't catch because vitest doesn't type-check.
Phase 74's desktop-e2e Windows leg failed, revealing a real base64/hex encoding bug in the SC#2 grant re-mint deliverable, blocking merge.
Git branch history from the overnight session ended up non-atomic (a file rename rode into the wrong commit) due to git mv pre-staging before splitting commits.
A crypto-review sub-agent lacked Edit tool access and could only report doc-fix findings rather than applying them directly.
User had to manually interrupt/redirect twice (once to git switch main and pull after a PR merged, once to stop the Phase 76 agent) since the autonomous loop doesn't detect these signals itself.
open_items: Fix Phase 74's SC#2 grant re-mint hex/base64 encoding bug (engine.rs:617) plus its unit test and shares.rs:93 doc, currently being fixed by a dispatched TDD agent.

Fix the dirty-resume rotatedNodes gap (medium security: repaired descendants after crash-resumed rotation keep stale in-memory read keys, latent revocation bypass) in both Rust and TS engines — logged as todo, now being addressed inline.
Fix the desktop-e2e Carol-retained assertion that derives a folder from a stale pre-rotation ref — logged as todo.
Server DTO codegen fix for share-response.dto.ts hex/base64 mislabeling (out of Phase-74 scope, requires pnpm api:generate + regenerated client).
Todo: re-mint trusts server for recipient-pubkey binding without independent verification (MEDIUM, inherited/newly-reachable) — logged, not fixed.
Todo: TS rotatedNodes defensive-copy parity with Rust's .clone() — logged, not fixed.

Cross-cutting hardening pass proposed (not yet started): named boundary codecs, branded hex/base64 string types, a wire-encoding contract doc, and a contract test asserting client output matches server DTO regex — to permanently prevent recurrence of the hex/base64 mixup across the codebase.
Phases 76, 78, 79 remain unplanned/unexecuted for milestone v2.0 closeout.
Phase 74 PR #607 remains unmerged pending gap-closure fixes and re-verification of the desktop-e2e leg.
Phase 77's live sdk-e2e round-trip for the TEE wire-field rename was not run (validated only via typecheck + both-side unit specs) — flagged as an optional deeper check before merge.
